about: Omara is a Chandigarh-based retail jewellery business selling designer natural-diamond jewellery under its own 'Omara' brand, primarily through a single retail boutique. Designs are developed in-house and manufactured by a product development and supply partner; it also offers customisation. Revenue was about 45.87 crore in FY26.

objects.purpose: Capex for renovation and expansion of the jewellery boutique (Chandigarh)
Marketing and promotional expenses to build the Omara brand
Repayment or prepayment of bank and financial institution borrowings

promoters.background: Promoters have experience in the gems and jewellery industry; Samarth Jaiswal is Managing Director and holds 99.12% pre-issue. No promoter shares are pledged.

concentration.note: Top customer was 16.33% of FY26 revenue (3.79% in FY25, 10.35% in FY24). Supplier concentration is high: top suppliers table shows 31.76% of purchases in FY26.

litigation_note: No outstanding criminal proceedings, regulatory actions or tax claims against the company as per the litigation chapter; no contingent liabilities. Materiality threshold Rs 20.68 lakh.
strengths: Fast growth: revenue roughly doubled to 45.87 crore in FY26 (up 95%) and PAT rose to 9.37 crore.
High reported returns: RoCE 85.38% and RoNW 74.78% in FY26.
Improving margins: EBITDA margin 31.45% and gross margin 39.58% in FY26.
Own 'Omara' brand with in-house designs and customisation for bridal and festive demand.
Products carry BIS hallmarking and GIA-type diamond certification, supporting trust.
Leverage falling: debt/equity improved from 26.35 in FY24 to 1.79 in FY26.
IPO proceeds of 18 crore earmarked to repay borrowings, cutting interest burden.
Premises on a registered 15-year lease to 2037 in Chandigarh.

risks.title: Negative operating cash flow
risks.detail: Operating cash flow was negative in all three years (-6.70 crore in FY26) as inventory and receivables grew; growth is funded by borrowings.

risks.title: High debt
risks.detail: Total debt was 22.43 crore in FY26 against net worth of 12.52 crore (debt/equity 1.79); finance cost 1.49 crore.

risks.title: Single-boutique, single-location business
risks.detail: Sales come primarily through one retail boutique in Chandigarh, so local demand, lease or premises issues can hurt the whole business.

risks.title: Supplier concentration
risks.detail: Dependent on a few suppliers for diamonds, gold and components; top suppliers table shows 31.76% of FY26 purchases from one tier, and jewellery is made by a single development and supply partner.

risks.title: Customer concentration and no obligation to buy
risks.detail: Top customer was 16.33% of FY26 revenue versus 3.79% in FY25; customers have no obligation to keep buying.

risks.title: Very rapid and uneven earnings growth
risks.detail: PAT margin jumped from 1.34% in FY24 to 20.42% in FY26 on a small base; revenue grew only 1.43% in FY25, so the sustainability of margins is uncertain.

risks.title: Late statutory filings
risks.detail: Many ROC filings (AOC-4, MGT-7A, DPT-3, DIR-12) were delayed by up to 1,275 days; additional fees were paid but future penalties cannot be ruled out.

risks.title: Promoter dominance and related-party dealings
risks.detail: Promoter Samarth Jaiswal holds 99.12% pre-issue (68.43% post); related-party sales, loans and unsecured loans from directors exist. Objects not appraised by any bank.
